labels.note: Encryption at rest contradicts plaintext storage of user preferences.
Encryption at rest contradicts administrator recovery of plaintext credential data; dissimilar-sounding pair per ADR-01 DR-10.
Same subject (API timeouts) with incompatible numeric constraints (2s vs 10s).
bcrypt hashing contradicts recoverable plaintext credentials; dissimilar-sounding pair per ADR-01 DR-10.
Both require support for multi-factor authentication; different wording only.
Both require persisting failed login attempts; 'record' vs 'retain in an audit log' is wording only.
Both require recording successful login attempts; different wording only.
Emailing a confirmation requires a verified email address to exist.
7-year retention is only satisfiable if retention periods are configurable per data category.
Password reset email depends on a stored verified email address for the user.
'Promptly' has no numeric bound; readers may assume wildly different timings.
'User-friendly' has no measurable criterion.
'Responsive user experience' is vague and non-measurable.
'Multiple document formats' does not enumerate which formats are required.
99.9% uptime lacks a measurement window (monthly, quarterly, annual).
'Account is modified' does not enumerate modification types or notification channel.
API timeout configuration and failed-login alerting — same domain, different subjects; included as a control.
Same expiry rule, different subjects (admin vs guest) — different scope, not a conflict.
Google OAuth is a refinement of OAuth2 support, not a conflict or dependency.
Logging failed logins and alerting after repeated failures are complementary behaviors.
Unrelated requirements (ID preservation vs file size limit); included as a control.
